title: Montréal

hotel.name: Alt Hotel Montréal
hotel.label: Booked
hotel.description: Your booked base in Griffintown, at Peel and Wellington, near Chez Potier and the Lachine Canal.

places.name: La Banquise
places.description: The flexible late-arrival poutine stop. Keep it casual tonight and save the nice meal for Saturday.
places.note: Check late kitchen hours before leaving the hotel.

places.name: St-Viateur Bagel
places.description: The original wood-fired bagel shop. Get a hot sesame bagel and watch the baking.
places.note: Original flagship at 263 Saint-Viateur West: published hours daily 6 AM–midnight. Counter-service bakery; no reservation.

places.name: Café Olimpico
places.description: Espresso and a lively neighborhood crowd. Pause here together after bagels rather than treating coffee as another quick errand.
places.note: Use the original Saint-Viateur location.

places.name: Bref
places.description: A bright gallery-boutique of ceramics, prints, and limited-edition design objects.
places.note: Saturday and Sunday 11 AM–5 PM on the contact page.

places.name: LVNEA
places.description: Locally made botanical perfumes: resins, woods, unusual atmospheric scents.
places.note: Entrance on Casgrain; published weekend hours 11 AM–6 PM.

places.name: Librairie Drawn & Quarterly
places.mapQuery: Librairie Drawn & Quarterly, 176 Rue Bernard Ouest
places.description: Art books, graphic novels, and good things to pick up and show each other.
places.note: On Bernard, by Bref and the record shops.

places.name: H Parfums
places.description: A polished niche-perfume boutique with independent houses to compare.
places.note: Saturday 10 AM–5 PM; Sunday noon–5 PM.

places.name: Schwartz’s Deli
places.description: Montréal smoked meat, mustard, and a pickle. Order medium-fat.
places.note: Use takeaway if the sit-down queue is long.

places.name: Habitat 67
places.description: A genuinely unusual stacked-housing experiment. A guided visit has more substance than a distant glance.
places.note: The 2026 tour calendar reaches Nov 22. Saturday slots are unverified; internal access requires a tour. Separate taxi trip across the water.

places.name: L’Express
places.description: A classic French bistro with a serious cellar and late service.
places.note: Reservations for two available online through Libro; larger parties by phone. Saturday check showed only midnight slots, not a 7 PM table.

places.name: Cloakroom Bar
places.mapQuery: Cloakroom Bar, 2175 Rue de la Montagne
places.description: An intimate, no-menu cocktail bar that builds a drink around the flavors you like.
places.note: 25 seats, no reservations. Ask the price before ordering rare spirits.

places.name: Crew Collective & Café
places.description: A spectacular former bank turned café. A proper place to sit, have coffee, and talk while enjoying the architecture.
places.note: A public café, not just coworking space. Tables can be busy; seating is not guaranteed.

places.name: Place d’Armes & Notre-Dame
places.description: The blue-and-gold basilica interior is much more striking than a quick look at the façade.
places.note: Daytime adult entry starts at CAD 16 + tax; AURA starts at CAD 37 + tax. Sunday sightseeing is 12:30–4 PM.

places.name: L’Empreinte coopérative
places.description: Québec-made ceramics, glass, jewelry, and artisan objects in an actual makers’ cooperative.
places.note: 88 Saint-Paul Est. Confirm seasonal November opening times.

places.name: Rue Saint-Paul → Old Port
places.description: Stone streets, river views, little passages, and a long waterfront promenade.
places.note: The exposed river edge is windy; the streets are an easy shorter loop.

places.name: Olive et Gourmando
places.mapQuery: Olive et Gourmando, 351 Rue Saint-Paul Ouest
places.description: A cozy old-city café for excellent sandwiches, baked goods, and a proper lunch.
places.note: 351 Saint-Paul Ouest; published weekends 8 AM–5 PM. Takeaway avoids a brunch wait.

places.name: Leméac
places.description: A more polished Outremont bistro for a long lunch or proper dinner.
places.note: Weekend brunch/lunch 10 AM–3 PM; dinner 5–11 PM. Reserve.

places.name: Pâtisserie Au Kouign-Amann
places.mapQuery: Pâtisserie Au Kouign-Amann, 316 Avenue du Mont-Royal Est
places.description: A slice of caramelized, buttery kouign-amann. Split one while it is warm.
places.note: Saturday option. Tastet lists Sunday closed.

places.name: North Star Machines à Piastres
places.mapQuery: North Star Machines à Piastres, 3908 Boulevard Saint-Laurent
places.description: Vintage pinball, a drink, and a little friendly competition.
places.note: Opposite the Schwartz’s stretch; machine noise, not a quiet lounge. Confirm hours.

places.name: Bota Bota
places.description: A floating hot-and-cold spa with river views. Keep this as an optional spa outing if you specifically want a quiet session.
places.note: Silence is required on the boat, so this is a weaker fit for a conversation-focused afternoon. Confirm conversation-permitted areas before booking. Swimsuit needed.

places.name: Cité Mémoire night walk
places.description: Local stories projected onto real buildings after dark. Try a couple on an evening walk.
places.note: Operator lists reopened scenes Wednesday–Sunday after nightfall. Check the current app map.

places.name: Ex-Voto
places.description: A well-curated mix of local clothing, ceramics, stationery, and home objects.
places.note: Pair with État de choc; both sit on the Saint-Laurent approach to Little Italy.

places.name: Bernie Beigne
places.description: Big, fluffy doughnuts and playful flavors. The fun sweet stop in this cluster.
places.note: Bernard Ouest. Check current hours and go before sell-outs.

places.name: Les chocolats de Chloé
places.mapQuery: Les chocolats de Chloé, 546 Avenue Duluth Est
places.description: Handmade chocolates, caramels, and crunchy chocolate-coated sponge toffee.
places.note: 546 Duluth Est; Saturday 11 AM–6 PM, Sunday 11 AM–5 PM.

places.name: Monarque · Brasserie
places.description: The upgraded dinner pick: a handsome room, polished service, and ambitious French cooking.
places.note: Book the brasserie, not the separate four-course dining room. Saturday service from 5 PM.

places.name: Chez Potier
places.description: The refined pastry stop: individual cakes, chocolate work, macarons, and beautiful seasonal desserts.
places.note: 630 Wellington; weekends 8 AM–5 PM. Excellent for pastries, but seating is limited: this is not the main long café break.

places.name: Bar George
places.description: Carved wood, stained glass, cocktails, and a grand mansion setting. Get a drink and the café gourmand.
places.note: The current menu lists five mini desserts for CAD 20. Bar seating is walk-in.

places.name: Ratafia
places.description: Inventive plated desserts with wine or cocktails. This is the dessert destination, not just a bakery stop.
places.note: Evening only, Tuesday–Saturday from 5 PM; closed Sunday. It replaces the evening plan, not a quick daytime detour.

places.name: État de choc
places.description: Bean-to-bar chocolates, tasting bars, and gifts that are actually worth bringing home.
places.note: 6466 Saint-Laurent; Saturday 10 AM–5 PM, Sunday 11 AM–5 PM.

places.name: Atrium Le 1000 · indoor skating
places.mapQuery: Atrium Le 1000, 1000 Rue De La Gauchetière Ouest
places.description: A year-round indoor rink beneath a glass atrium, downtown and north of your Griffintown hotel.
places.note: Official Sunday hours 11:30 AM–6 PM. Timed-arrival tickets are recommended; availability is not guaranteed.

places.name: MONOKIINI · ceramics & café
places.description: Handmade ceramics, a café, and makers working in the studio.
places.note: Boutique visit and coffee, not a booked workshop.

places.name: atelier b · workshop boutique
places.description: Locally made natural-fiber clothing plus jewelry, ceramics, and other makers’ work, with the workshop behind the shop.
places.note: Saturday 11 AM–5 PM.

places.name: WACHIYA · Cree artisan objects
places.description: Authentic Cree beadwork, jewelry, sculpture, and handmade objects from Eeyou Istchee.
places.note: 79 Saint-Paul East, opposite L’Empreinte. Published listings show Wednesday–Sunday 10 AM–6 PM.

places.name: Galerie Noël Guyomarc’h
places.description: Contemporary art jewelry and sculptural objects by independent makers. A more unusual browse than a conventional luxury jeweler.
places.note: Published Saturday hours 11 AM–5 PM; closed Sunday. Images are archive gallery photographs, not current inventory.

places.name: Clark Street Mercantile
places.description: Independent menswear, accessories, and useful design objects chosen for craftsmanship. A relaxed, considered shop with its own label and a roster including Portuguese Flannel, orSlow, Universal Works, Kinto, and Snow Peak.
places.note: 5200 Clark. Current contact page: Saturday 11 AM–6 PM.
places.coordinate_verification: Named OSM shop at street number5200 on Rue Clark, matching official address; coordinates retrieved via Photon.

places.name: Les Faiseurs
places.description: Handmade Québec ceramics, specialty coffee, and pastries.
places.note: Saturday 9 AM–6 PM. Walk-in café and browsing.

places.name: Galerie LeRoyer
places.description: Contemporary paintings and sculpture in a Saint-Paul gallery.
places.note: Sunday 10 AM–6 PM. Free browsing; exhibitions rotate.

places.name: Place Carmin
places.description: Bright French brasserie with weekend brunch and Sunday lunch.
places.note: Sunday 10 AM–2:30 PM. Reserve a dining-room table.

places.name: Maison Sauvage
places.address: 162 Rue Bernard O, Montréal, QC H2T 2K2
places.hours_note: Current RestoMontreal listing corroborated by current local listings; owner Instagram could not be independently read.
places.blurb: Optional hot-chocolate and cookie stop near Bref. Order the rich Viennese Choco Deluxe with homemade vanilla whipped cream. Small room, limited seating; stop in if a seat is free.
places.seating_note: A photographed upholstered bench and window counters exist, but the current venue description explicitly says seating is limited and weekends are busy. Do not frame as a guaranteed long comfortable hangout.
places.photo_note: Three genuine venue photographs: interior, signature meringue drinks with cookies, and an illustrative past lemon-meringue cookie. No photo is mislabeled as hot chocolate; exact cookie flavors vary.

places.name: La Bête à Pain · Griffintown
places.mapQuery: La Bête à Pain Griffintown, 195 Rue Young
places.description: French pastries and Callebaut hot chocolate in an airy café with 35 seats.
places.note: Saturday and Sunday 8 AM–6 PM.

blocks.title: Alt Hotel Montréal
blocks.text: Booked · 120 Rue Peel, Griffintown. Taxi from YUL; notify reception of late arrival.

blocks.title: St-Viateur Bagel
blocks.text: Hot wood-fired sesame bagels from the original bakery.

nearby.text: Viennese-style dark hot chocolate with vanilla whipped cream, plus elaborate cookies. Upholstered seating; limited space.

blocks.title: Bref
blocks.text: Independent ceramics, prints, and small-run design objects.

nearby.text: Independent bookshop on Bernard: art books, graphic novels, and small publishers.

blocks.title: H Parfums
blocks.text: Niche fragrances from independent perfume houses.

nearby.text: Art jewelry and sculptural objects on Saint-Laurent. Saturday 11 AM–5 PM.

blocks.title: Leméac
blocks.text: French bistro lunch. CAD 55–90 each before tax and tip.
blocks.note: Reserve for two; 12:30 PM was available Nov 18.

blocks.title: LVNEA
blocks.text: Locally made botanical perfume: woods, resins, and unusual scents. Entrance on Casgrain.

nearby.text: Independent menswear, accessories, and design objects chosen for craftsmanship. 5200 Clark; Saturday 11 AM–6 PM.

blocks.title: État de choc
blocks.text: Bean-to-bar chocolate and bonbons to take home.

nearby.text: Québec ceramics, specialty coffee, and pastries. A walk-in browse or café stop on Saint-Laurent.

blocks.title: MONOKIINI
blocks.text: Handmade ceramics, a working studio, and coffee.

blocks.title: Alt Hotel Montréal
blocks.text: Taxi back, drop shopping, and take a break.

nearby.text: Near Alt: French pastries and Callebaut hot chocolate. Bright, airy café with 35 seats.

blocks.title: Atrium Le 1000
blocks.text: Indoor skating beneath a glass atrium. Entry + skates + helmet: about CAD 23.
blocks.note: Book the 4:30–5:30 PM arrival window; arrive around 5 PM.

blocks.title: Monarque
blocks.text: French brasserie dinner. CAD 85–130 each before tax and tip.

nearby.text: Free projections on Old Montréal’s walls after dark; near Monarque.

blocks.note: No brasserie tables listed Nov 18. Formal dining room: 9:30 PM available. Alternatives below.

blocks.title: Cloakroom
blocks.text: Small cocktail bar; drinks tailored to your taste. Taxi back to Alt afterward.

nearby.text: Ornate mansion bar near Cloakroom. Walk-in cocktails; separate from Alt.

blocks.note: Walk-in only. Go before dinner if choosing Monarque at 9:30 PM.

blocks.title: Crew Collective & Café
blocks.text: Breakfast and coffee in a grand former bank. Leave bags at Alt before heading out.

blocks.title: L’Empreinte
blocks.text: Québec-made ceramics, glass, and jewelry in an artisan cooperative.

blocks.title: Old Port
blocks.text: A waterfront walk along the quays and old streets.

nearby.text: Free contemporary art and sculpture browse on Saint-Paul West. Sunday 10 AM–6 PM; exhibitions rotate.

blocks.title: Place d’Armes & Notre-Dame
blocks.text: The square and the basilica’s blue-and-gold interior. Admission from CAD 16 + tax.

nearby.text: Sandwiches, pastries, and a sit-down lunch. Walk-in; expect a queue.

blocks.note: Book daytime admission, separate from AURA.

blocks.title: Place Carmin
blocks.text: Sunday lunch in a bright, polished French brasserie. Choose from the weekend menu; leave room for pastry afterward.
blocks.note: Dining-room tables for two at 1:30 PM were available Nov 18. Reserve.

blocks.title: Chez Potier
blocks.text: French pastry for dessert: try a Paris-Brest, millefeuille, or chocolate éclair. Limited seating.

blocks.title: Alt Hotel Montréal
blocks.text: Walk back from Chez Potier and collect bags.

blocks.title: Taxi to YUL
blocks.text: Leave Alt at 4 PM; target the airport by 5 PM.

blocks.title: Flights home
blocks.text: Milo: AC736 → LaGuardia 9:30 PM. Forrest: AC8612 → Boston 9:28 PM.

practical.title: Getting around
practical.text: Walk within each area. Taxi to the northern shops and back Saturday, and to YUL Sunday.

neighborhoods.name: Mile End & Outremont
neighborhoods.subtitle: Coffee, independent design, perfume, and a polished bistro. Your Saturday morning cluster.

neighborhoods.name: The Plateau
neighborhoods.subtitle: Lunch, handmade chocolates, a great pastry, and a short game of pinball. Walk between these stops.

neighborhoods.name: Old Montréal & the river
neighborhoods.subtitle: The main afternoon and Sunday cluster. Chez Potier is at the western edge; Habitat 67 needs a taxi across the water.

neighborhoods.name: Golden Square Mile
neighborhoods.subtitle: Two polished evening stops near the downtown hotels. A taxi transfer from Old Montréal.

neighborhoods.name: Little Italy · the dessert detour
neighborhoods.subtitle: North of Mile End, so treat this as a separate cluster. Ratafia is an evening destination; chocolate and shopping work in the day.

hotels.name: Le Germain Montréal
hotels.label: Easy default
hotels.description: Refined, comfortable, and central. The cleanest shared-room choice.

hotels.name: Hôtel William Gray
hotels.label: Best old-city atmosphere
hotels.description: Stone architecture, contemporary rooms, and a real hotel living room. Best if you want the hotel to feel part of the trip.
hotels.beds: Confirm a two-bed category; many rooms are kings.

hotels.name: Alt Hotel Montréal
hotels.label: Booked
hotels.description: Your booked base in Griffintown, at Peel and Wellington, near Chez Potier and the Lachine Canal.

hotels.name: Hôtel Nelligan
hotels.label: Warm, romantic old stone
hotels.description: Brick, beams, and a cozy Old Montréal base. A good counterpoint to the modern downtown hotels.
hotels.beds: Confirm the current two-bed room category directly.

reservations.name: Saturday dinner
reservations.status: No brasserie tables listed Nov 18. Formal dining room: 9:30 PM available. Call +1 514 875-3896 for cancellations.

reservations.name: Atrium skating
reservations.status: Arrive around 5 PM. Add skate and helmet rentals.

cocktails: Cloakroom and Bar George: walk-in only.
